title: Tree Component Count
summary: Count connected components that are trees in an undirected multigraph.
statement: Count connected components that are trees in an undirected multigraph. Implement `tree_component_count` and return the required result without changing the callable signature.
constraints: Inputs follow the declared Python and JSON-compatible types.
Return a deterministic result for every valid input.
hints: A connected undirected component is a tree exactly when edges equal vertices minus one.
Traverse each component while counting vertices and paired adjacency entries.
Pseudocode checkpoint: identify the state, update it once per step, and return only after the tree_component_count invariant is complete.
Editorial: Traverse each component while counting vertices and paired adjacency entries. The intended bounds are O(V+E) time and O(V) space.
editorial: A connected undirected component is a tree exactly when edges equal vertices minus one. Traverse each component while counting vertices and paired adjacency entries. This yields O(V+E) time and O(V) auxiliary space.

tests.explanation: The first component is a tree; the second contains a cycle, so only one component counts.
Each isolated node is an acyclic connected component, so all three count as trees.
